To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distributed camera approach for head movement estimation is a viable option for driver assistance systems, with a particular emphasis on the ability for continuous tracking during large head movements away and back to the frontal pose.

a distributed camera framework is a promising approach to robustly estimate the head pose and head dynamics even during spatially large head motions, and that a 3-D head model can be used to improve the robustness and accuracy of head pose estimation.

(1) a distributed camera system is necessary to robustly estimate head pose and dynamics, (2) the proposed system is robust to large head movements, and (3) the system can detect interesting events (such as a lane change) with a good accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing robust head movement estimation algorithms and evaluating them in realistic driving scenarios.
a robust and continuous estimation of the head pose and movement in a driving context.
developing a robust head pose estimator that is capable of continuous and accurate head pose tracking even under large head movements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the distributed camera framework is more accurate than the single camera system, and the distributed camera framework with a single camera at the driver's side is more accurate than that of two cameras at the front.
the proposed distributed camera framework is capable of providing a robust and accurate estimate of the head pose and movement even in the presence of spatially large head movement.
the distributed camera framework provides robustness and continuous operation even during large head motions, which is not possible with a single camera.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distributed camera system can be a viable alternative to the single-camera system for head pose and dynamics estimation, particularly when the camera is located at the rear view mirror.
the proposed framework can robustly and continuously track a driver's head pose and dynamics even in nonfrontal glances.
we have presented a robust, distributed head pose estimator, which is capable of continuous operation during large head movements, and evaluated the system on a new head movement data set.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed distributed camera framework can provide a robust and reliable estimation of head movement dynamics in a wide range of head movement conditions, which is critical for driver monitoring systems.
a robust head movement analysis system can be developed by exploiting the constraints of a driving context and the data collected in such a context.
the proposed distributed camera system is robust to large head movements and can be applied to real-world scenarios.
